history.summary: About 2.5 km west of the Jagannath Temple, this is one of the five famous Shiva temples of Puri (the others: Markandeswara, Jambeswar, Banambara, Kapalamochana). Legend says Lord Rama, en route to Sri Lanka, vowed to worship Shiva here; villagers of Sabarapalli gave him a pumpkin (lau/lauka) shaped like a Shiva linga, which he installed - hence 'Laukanatha', later Sanskritised to 'Lokanatha'. The presiding linga sits submerged year-round in natural spring water inside the sanctum (said to be the Ganga flowing through it); the water is bailed out only on the night of Pankoddhar Ekadashi, three days before Shivaratri, when thousands come for darshan. The water mixed with offerings is taken as medicated prasad believed to cure diseases. The utsava murti (festival icon) of Lokanath is kept inside the Jagannath temple, where he is the guardian deity of Lord Jagannath's treasures and jewellery.

name: Lokanath Temple
town_description: Puri is a major coastal city in Odisha on the Bay of Bengal, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage destinations and home to the Shree Jagannath Temple. It is also known for its beaches, the annual Rath Yatra that draws millions, and the nearby Konark Sun Temple (about 35 km).
